keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for a state Cliopatria lacks: its Great Jin shape of 1206-1215 covers Manchuria (326 thousand km2 of Heilongjiang, 262 thousand of Jilin and all of Primorye) and the 1216 shape drops it, so there is no shape for Manchuria in 1216-1233. 'Established in Manchuria (including Northeast China and Outer Manchuria) ... in 1215'; the pages give no area. The shape is Jilin, Heilongjiang and Primorye, as the great-jin dossier reads the 1215 loss (confidence 2). Fixed after review: the capital Dongjing (Liaoyang, 123.18 E 41.28 N) lay outside Manchuria, so a 60 km Liaoyang disc is added for 1215-1216; the Eastern Liao page has Yelu Liuge occupy the same city in 1215, so the disc is a contested zone (contest 1215-1217 below).

The Laoyeling Mountains are not in the gazetteer, so the northern limit is not drawn beyond Manchuria (confidence 1).

ledger.note: 1215: Puxian Wannu founds the Eastern Xia. 'Established in Manchuria (including Northeast China and Outer Manchuria) by the Jurchen warlord Puxian Wannu in 1215'; 'founded the Eastern Xia dynasty in Dongjing (Liaoyang) in 1215 with the support of the Mongols'. The Puxian Wannu page: 'declared his independence in Liaodong' after the Mongols took Zhongdu in 1215 and 'founded a new state called Great Zhen'. The Jin sent him to Liaodong in 1214 and he was 'defeated around Kaiyuan'.

notes:
State Cliopatria lacks. Cliopatria's Great Jin shape of 1206-1215 covers Manchuria and the 1216 shape drops it; the great-jin dossier carries the 1215 loss to this slug at confidence 1 (the Xuanzong page it cites gave no year); the Eastern Xia page now dates the founding to 1215 and the land to Manchuria, so that event could be raised to 3 by the reviewer.

Extent. The pages give no area. 'Manchuria (including Northeast China and Outer Manchuria)' is read as Jilin, Heilongjiang and Primorye; the 1217 sentence adds Hamgyong-namdo ('south to Hamgyongnamdo') and a northern limit at the Laoyeling Mountains, which the gazetteer lacks. Kaiyuan (where Wannu was beaten in 1214) is not in the gazetteer. Liaoning is left to the eastern-liao dossier although the Eastern Xia page puts the founding at Dongjing (Liaoyang) in 1215, the year the Eastern Liao page has Yelu Liuge occupying the Jin's eastern capital; the pages do not reconcile this.

Names and dates. The Eastern Xia page calls the state Eastern Xia from the start; the Puxian Wannu page has Great Zhen in 1215 and Eastern Xia from 1217. The Eastern Xia page dates Liuge's Khitan revolt 1211, the Eastern Liao page 1212. No page gives a later Xia remnant after 1233. The Mongol vassalage (hostage Tege sent 'as a vassal' in 1216; the 1217 revolt; submission again by 1218; the 1222 revolt) is not a ledger event here: vassal events belong to the suzerain's dossier (mongol-empire, another group) with this slug as counterpart; the years are in the wars and in the notes above.

Fix round after review (2026-10-19): Dongjing (Liaoyang), the capital of 1215-1216, is now inside the 1215 keyframe as a 60 km disc, recorded as a contest with eastern-liao for 1215-1217 (Eastern Liao page: Yelu Liuge occupied the same city in 1215; Puxian Wannu page: he left it in 1217). The matching contest pair is NOT in the eastern-liao dossier (verdict fix, not touched in this round): eastern-liao needs contest_start 1215 and contest_end 1217 over {place: Liaoyang, km: 60} with counterpart eastern-xia. The 1217 gain of Hamgyong-namdo stays at confidence 1: the Puxian Wannu page, re-opened, names no previous holder and dates the sentence only under 1217. The Mongol vassalage (hostage 1216, revolts 1217 and 1222) is for mongol-empire (ia-02): that dossier has no eastern-xia event.
